strengths: FALCON addresses an important continual semantic segmentation problem: retaining old classes while learning under class imbalance and separating future classes within the background. Combining persistent prototypes, multiple unknown clusters, and learned cluster assignment is a potentially useful contribution.

The reported empirical gains cover three datasets, multiple incremental schedules, and CNN and Transformer architectures. For example, DeepLab-V3 reaches 36.4 mIoU versus FairCL's 34.7 on ADE20K 100-10, 62.41 versus SSUL's 59.25 on VOC 10-1, and 55.24 versus FairCL's 49.22 on Cityscapes 1-1 (Tables 6–8). This breadth supports the practical value of the overall system.

The ablations provide meaningful evidence of improved minority-class performance. On ADE20K 100-50, the fairness loss raises minority mIoU from 26.4 to 30.8 while majority mIoU rises from 51.5 to 52.1 (Table 1), narrowing the performance gap. Updating the visual grammar also improves over keeping it fixed, from 35.6 to 37.9 overall mIoU (Table 2).

Table 5 supports effective retention on the reported ADE20K 100-10 sequence: initial-class mIoU decreases only from 44.9 to 44.4 across subsequent tasks. The appendix provides useful optimizer and prototype-update settings and sensitivity studies for the scaling factor, cluster margin, neighborhood size, and backbone.
weaknesses: The core objective and its optimization contain unresolved inconsistencies that substantially affect reproducibility. Equation (8) optimizes network parameters, whereas prototypes are frozen or updated through momentum; Section 9 explicitly treats them as constants. Under this description, the prototype-only regularizer R_C(c) has no gradient to the network, leaving the improvements attributed to it in Table 4 unexplained. Also, Proposition 2 requires the transition vector v to participate in the shared softmax denominator, but Equation (4) inherits a denominator defined over feature samples without specifying that inclusion. Without it, the stated loss is unbounded below in unconstrained v.

The central fairness interpretation does not follow from the propositions. The quantity ℓ_i is a normalized softmax mass, not a measure of geometric compactness. Its optimum 1/L changes with sample count even when every feature remains identical to its centroid. Consequently, Proposition 1 does not establish that minority features are more scattered, and Proposition 2's probability-mass adjustment does not establish improved compactness or prediction fairness. Separately, Appendix 9 invokes a metric triangle inequality without establishing that the actual contrastive loss satisfies it, so the claimed knowledge-distillation bound is unsupported.

The ablations do not fully isolate the proposed mechanisms. Table 1 changes both the contrastive-loss scale and the transition-vector term without an α-scaled vanilla-loss control, leaving their contributions unresolved. Table 4 simultaneously removes visual grammar and reduces the number of unknown clusters to one; Table 2 does not clearly establish a comparison with the same number of unknown clusters. Thus, the evidence does not cleanly distinguish learned assignment from the benefit of allowing multiple clusters. These distinctions matter when assessing the contribution beyond the cited parametric contrastive learning and Clusformer components.

Several consequential implementation details remain unspecified even in the appendix: the ImageNet pretraining procedure for the visual grammar, DBSCAN radius and minimum-sample settings, and the procedure for separating old-class pixels from unknown candidates within unlabeled background. Computational usefulness is also difficult to assess because training time and memory overhead are not reported despite the auxiliary 12-layer Transformer and repeated feature-extraction stages.

There are secondary reporting errors: Table 3(a) uses VOC class ranges for ADE20K, and Table 6 reports 23.5 old-class, 10.6 new-class, and 26.6 overall mIoU for Mask2Former MiB on ADE20K 100-10, which is inconsistent with an overall class mean. These are correctable issues. My Weak Reject recommendation is driven primarily by the unresolved objective/optimization definitions and unsupported central theoretical interpretation, which currently outweigh the substantial empirical merits.
